classification.difficultyReason: Applies the chain rule to a shrinking sphere and interprets a negative derivative.

content.prompt:
A spherical snowball is melting in such a way that its radius is decreasing at a rate of 0.5 cm/min.
At what rate is the volume of the snowball decreasing when the radius is 3 cm?
Give your answer in exact form.

answer.worked:
$$V=\frac43\pi r^3,\qquad \frac{dr}{dt}=-\frac12\text{ cm/min}.$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dV}{dt}&=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=4\pi r^2\left(-\frac12\right)\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-2\pi r^2.\end{align*}$$
When $r=3$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dV}{dt}&=-2\pi(3)^2\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=-18\pi\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}.\end{align*}$$
The volume is decreasing at $18\pi\text{ cm}^3/\text{min}$.
